articles.title: A renamed cookie and a logout button that did nothing
articles.excerpt: After the first review I renamed the session cookie to __Host-session. The prefix makes the browser accept the cookie only over HTTPS, with no domain attribute and with the path set to the root, which…
articles.body: After the first review I renamed the session cookie to __Host-session. The prefix makes the browser accept the cookie only over HTTPS, with no domain attribute and with the path set to the root, which closes a few ways of planting a fake session. Login and the password change both started using the new name. The logout code kept the old one. It read a cookie called session, found nothing, deleted nothing on the server and cleared a cookie that no longer existed. The Exit button redirected to the login page and looked as if it had worked. The session row in the database stayed valid, and so did the cookie in the browser, for up to 14 days. On a salon computer that two people share, the second person would open the clients page and be logged in as the first. Every automated test passed.

articles.title: Reading a webhook debugging prompt line by line
articles.excerpt: Webhook bugs are awkward to hand to an AI. The symptom shows up in one place, while the cause sits in delivery order, retries or a recent change somewhere else. This is a teardown of a prompt from the…
articles.body: Webhook bugs are awkward to hand to an AI. The symptom shows up in one place, while the cause sits in delivery order, retries or a recent change somewhere else. This is a teardown of a prompt from the PromptAlo community library built for exactly that: Finding Why Third-Party Webhook Events Arrive Out of Order. The Solves line Solves: Backend developers whose app breaks when webhooks arrive late, twice or in the wrong order. Three failure modes in one sentence: late, duplicated and reordered. Naming all of them matters, because a fix for order alone will not stop the same event being processed again. The fill-in line Fill in these variables: [APP], [FLOW], [SYMPTOMS], [RETRIES], [LOGS], [CHANGES] [FLOW] is the field that shapes the answer.

articles.title: I built a PDF toolkit that never uploads your files
articles.excerpt: Every "free" PDF converter I tried asked me to upload the file first. For a bank statement or a signed contract, that is the whole problem: you are handing a document to a server you know nothing abou…
articles.body: Every "free" PDF converter I tried asked me to upload the file first. For a bank statement or a signed contract, that is the whole problem: you are handing a document to a server you know nothing about, and hoping it gets deleted. So I built ConvUp , a converter that runs entirely in the browser. No upload endpoint, no account, no watermark. What is actually possible in a browser today More than I expected. The stack: pdf-lib — create, merge, split, rotate, number pages, draw text, embed images. pdf.js — render pages to canvas for JPG export and for OCR input. Tesseract.js — OCR in a Web Worker, with the language model cached after first use. JSZip — build .docx and .zip files client-side. Web Audio + a Worker — decode and re-encode audio to MP3/WAV.

articles.title: I Played Three Mobile Games to Find the Math Hiding Inside Them
articles.excerpt: By Bulamba Isimbi Melissa Games feel like pure fun, but every jump, camera swing and score counter is powered by math. For a class assignment I stopped playing like a player and started playing like a…
articles.body: By Bulamba Isimbi Melissa Games feel like pure fun, but every jump, camera swing and score counter is powered by math. For a class assignment I stopped playing like a player and started playing like a developer. I analysed three free mobile games: Subway Surfers and Vector from the recommended list, and Temple Run as my own pick. I looked for six ideas from class: distance, vectors, algebra, dot product, cross product and linear interpolation (lerp). I can’t see the source code, so what follows is based on what I observed. Where I’m inferring how something works, I say “likely”. I played each game for at least 30 minutes across 12 sessions, took screenshots and wrote notes as I went.

articles.title: Peanuts Native brings 12 Switch games to Android without an emulator layer
articles.excerpt: The open-source translation layer builds on BananaNative, and supports dual-screen Android handhelds.
articles.body: Credit: AYN TL;DR Peanuts Native is a new open-source fork of BananaNative that converts 12 Nintendo Switch games into standalone Android apps without a traditional emulator layer. Created by the developer behind Eden Duo, it supports dual-screen Android handhelds like the AYN Thor by rendering interactive companion overlays with haptic feedback on the bottom display. Converting legally dumped game files takes five to 40 minutes on-device and requires Android 13 or later, at least 12GB of RAM, and a Snapdragon GPU with Vulkan 1.3 support. It’s an exciting time to be an Android emulation fan. Not only is the emulation scene moving quickly lately, but native recompilation projects are also speeding up, letting you bypass the emulator layer to run console titles “natively” on Android.

articles.title: 'Don't panic': SpaceX pens familiar message on Starship ahead of historic double-catch test flight
articles.excerpt: SpaceX has inked a familiar phrase on the Starship rocket that will fly a historic mission today (Nov. 13) — "Don't panic." And the company has invoked those words before.
articles.body: SpaceX has a message for itself, and for the spacecraft set to make history today (Nov. 13): Don't panic. The company's Starship megarocket will conduct its 15th test flight this afternoon, a landmark liftoff that will feature the first-ever attempt to catch both of its stages with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms. On Thursday (Nov. 12), SpaceX rolled the Flight 15 upper stage, a vehicle known as Ship 42, out to the launch pad at its Starbase site in South Texas to prep. The company shared photos of the move on X , and in two of those shots we can see some intriguing words inked on the spacecraft: "Don't panic." Another look at Ship 42 at the pad on Nov. 12.
articles.author: Mike Wall

articles.title: Watch SpaceX attempt a historic Starship launch and double-catch landing today (Nov. 13)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented double-catch mission today (Nov. 13), and you can watch the action live.
articles.body: SpaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented mission today (Nov. 13), and you can watch the action live. Starship is scheduled to launch on its 15th test flight today from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). SpaceX plans to bring both of Starship's stages back to Starbase for a catch by the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — something it has never done before. You can watch it all live here at Space.com. And there should be a lot to see: Starship Flight 15 will last more than 22 hours, if all goes according to plan.
